concepts.name: Why DRAM is Slow
facts: DRAM is slow because of weak storage signals, slow sensing, destructive reads, and large dense arrays.

DRAM stores bits as tiny capacitor charges producing only a small voltage difference on long bitlines, which the sense amplifier must detect and amplify. Reading disturbs the stored charge so data must be restored after every row activation, and capacity-focused arrays have long rows and bitlines.

Sensing takes time: the sense amp must amplify a very small voltage change.
